correctness.rationale: The complete proof derives the six Jordan partitions from a valid coordinate automorphism for nonzero linear terms, exact 2x2 leading multiplication matrices for nonzero quadratic terms, the identity \(f^2=(b^2-ac)x^2y^2\), and explicit cubic/quartic ideal images. Cone counts hold for every finite field of characteristic three. Unit-group orbit sizes rigorously convert element counts to distinct principal-ideal counts. The six reduced rank loci are explicit smooth geometrically irreducible varieties. Reconstructed monomial matrices verify all 6561 radical elements and distinct principal ideals over F3, with 1064 direct F9 samples.

value.rationale: Multiplication Jordan types in a modular group algebra and dimensions of its principal ideals are intrinsic natural invariants. This is a complete all-element census at the first noncyclic odd-prime group algebra, not an arbitrarily chosen subset. The discriminant cone provides a structural explanation of a missing rank, while the total count of all principal ideals, \(3(q^2+q+1)+1\), is a nontrivial arithmetic invariant with an explicit geometric stratum refinement. The result may help benchmark ideal and modular Jordan invariants in larger truncated polynomial group algebras.
